newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe sees positive economic signs.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe sees positive economic signs.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Thursday he saw encouraging signs in the economy and insisted he planned no change in government policies, saying they were backed by President Jacques Chirac and parliament.
"Should we change policies? My answer is no," Juppe told a meeting of the Club de la Bourse, an association whose members include journalists and stock brokers.

Juppe, who on Wednesday won an unenthusiastic vote of confidence from parliament where his centre-right coalition controls four-fifths of the seats, said he was wedded to current policies "by conviction and not out of stubbornness".
His government has proposed unpopular steep spending and job cuts in its 1997 budget to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
The austerity programme has generated labour unrest and a wave of strikes as unemployment rose to record levels in August while economic growth remained sluggish.
It has also generated considerable criticism from within the majority.
But Juppe said he saw "encouraging signs" in the economy, including "solid fundamentals, inflation under control, good foreign trade and falling rates".
He urged an end to the French people's gloomy mood, which he said was paralysing consumption and investment.

His policies had the "unambiguous support of the president (Jacques Chirac) and of the parliamentary majority," he said though his approval rating is near to an all-time low at 30 percent and Chirac had to intervene twice in the last week to shield him from criticism within the coalition.
